summary: Principal individual contributor for the Scheduling Core team: sets technical direction for the booking engine and the waitlist, keeps bookings correct under load, leads the design of waitlist backfill, and works with Integrations on HL7 and FHIR interfaces to clinic record systems. No direct reports; mentors across two teams and shares on-call.
team: Scheduling Core owns the booking engine, slot availability, the waitlist and the rules for who is offered a freed slot. Integrations, the sister team, owns connections to clinic record systems. A team of 8 engineers, a product manager and a designer.
interviewFormat: Technical panel with Ciaran Delahunt, Niamh Abara, Seun Adeyemi-Clarke and Petra Vondrak, Tue May 19 2026, 14:00 Irish time: systems you have built, then system design on waitlist backfill. Before it a recruiter screen; after it a director round of 45 minutes. No AI assistants in live interviews.

prepNotes: Round: technical panel, Tue May 19, 14:00 Irish time; Ciaran Delahunt, Niamh Abara, Seun Adeyemi-Clarke, Petra Vondrak; past systems, then system design on waitlist backfill; judges reasoning about failure modes.

Tell me about yourself: 17 years; booking, scheduling and integration work in health; principal at Lanternfield Health, 2.4 million appointments a year; before that the Wrenfield Clinics migration and Quillmere Labs.
Why Tidewell: the same problem at about five times the scale; scheduling and record-system integration side by side; waitlist and rota work in one place.
Double booking: Lanternfield Health, keys on the write path plus a database constraint; backup Brackenridge Hotels, the inventory row lock; never trust a client to send a request once.
HL7 and FHIR: Quillmere Labs first, the result router; then Lanternfield Health, six record systems behind one adapter contract.
Kubernetes: Wrenfield Clinics, the move off hand-built machines; Lanternfield Health for running it day to day.
Single sign-on: Wrenfield Dental Group, directory accounts for front-desk staff; say plainly it was one identity provider.
Rota and OR-Tools: Calderwick Rota, the roster generator; hard rules never broken, soft rules scored; I have not used OR-Tools itself.
Kafka and ordering: Quillmere Labs, the replayable result log; Wrenfield Clinics reminders; key by patient so one patient's events stay in order.
Migration: Wrenfield Clinics, 212 clinics in nine waves, dual run, parity report; contrast Wrenfield Dental Group, 38 practices in one weekend, and what that taught me.
Failure: Wrenfield Dental Group weekend cutover; 600 hygienist slots double-booked, 1.3% manual fixes; own it, then the wave rule.
Conflict: Wrenfield Clinics; the head of clinical operations wanted no cutovers in flu season; agreed freeze windows and a rollback rule instead of a three-month stop.
Deadline: Quillmere Labs; ten weeks to the critical-result rule; cut two report formats, kept the alert path; three days to spare.
Reminders and no-shows: Wrenfield Clinics, 11.5% to 9.4%; Pendlecross Pharmacy, forty percent fewer uncollected prescriptions; consent and quiet hours first.
On-call and SLOs: Lanternfield Health; 99.95% booking availability; pager one week in six; the error budget decides whether features or fixes ship.
PHI and audit: Corbel Mutual audit trail; Lanternfield Health access logs per field; least data in events. Answer shape: context, my part, decision, trade-off, result; two minutes.
